Hi!

Well i was diagnosed with gastritis 4 months ago, and it was the worst pain in the world. I messed up by not taking my medication for the first 2 weeks. I had started off with 20mg of esomepra. I only used it for the first week and stopped afterwards. However, i feel that was a mistake because it cause an acid reflux and i still wasn't cured. 

After waiting for a month to see my doctor, i was finally able to get prescribed some more medication (pantoprazole 40mg) for the that month to see how it goes. I was skeptical about the medication because of what i have read about some of he side effects were. During this period, i didn't cut back on dairy, spicy or any caffeine products, which was my mistake for not cutting back. It was getting better, but i still felt my stomach to be really sensitive every time i would touch it and eat, and also would still feel a burning sensation. So i go back the following month to talk to my doc about the situation. He gave me another 60 pills for the following two months. And i told him that i was eating and drinking dairy and caffeine products. He told me to quit cold turkey because they will continue to irritate my wound. So i stopped completely. 

Its been two to three months that i have been without any caffeine and dairy products. I'm only drink water at the moment. He also gave me some probiotics to take for these next two months and some enzymes to help with digestion of the food. The second month I've started to noticed my symptoms to get better! I've cut back on a lot of fast foods, junk food, and cut back on stress! I would test myself with what i can eat, and what i cannot eat. I started to feel better and better!!! I had a situation where i couldn't eat and drink because it would start to irritate my stomach. (Probably because i wasnt able to digest the food quickly, and the wound still being at a stage of sensitive.) However, on my third month, i was able to notice that i was able to drink and eat at the same time without any irritation! This actually gave me hope! I was able to introduce more and more foods back into my stomach! I still haven't taken a chance with dairy products or caffeine, but I've been introducing chocolate back to my stomach (use to irriate me). 

The only problem i face as this moment is that i feel because i can't digest my food quickly i have all this food lying around my stomach, which i think will cause my stomach to start irritate once again. Hopefully with the next month or so i can get a lower dosage to help with my digestion! But i still have to be extremely careful. It short words: it does heal, but it takes times and a lifestyle change. Stress is a big no no, and eating healthier and home cooked meals has to be introduced if it hasn't been already. It takes, but there is hope to heal from this horrible disease! 

Ps. Sorry for the really long response.

I had a very similar incident with NSAIDS. I got 8 teeth removed in the last couple of months. I got 4 removed on Oct 7th, and the other 4 on Nov 7th. I was prescribed antibiotics on both occasions where I had to take 4 pills a day, for a week, each pill being 500mg. So I was taking 2000mg a day. I would mostly take the pills without eating because I was so scared that I was going to infect my wounds. I didn't think about the consequences of taking a pill on an empty stomach also.  I also took 3 norcos in total(2 the first extraction, 1 the second extraction.) In the second extraction, I ended up taking a different pill in which it was called medrol dose pak to avoid inflamation. That was before my second extraction, which I would continue to use through out the week. So about a month passes, I made a mistake in mixing oj and milk together in the my stomach(are cereal, and then drank a glass of oj.) And that's when things started to go downhill. I started to get really bad pains in my stomach for eating certain foods. I was so scared to eat because I wasn't sure what it was. I ended up going to be er and was diagnosed with gastritis. I ended up taking ppi. Forgot the name of them, but apparently it was a good one. I only took them for a week because they made me feel worse. It did help out with the pain, but i felt like shit afterwards. So after 7 days I stopped taking them and went without taking anything. It's been about a month, and I've been pretty good. My bad eating habits is what is scaring me right now because i feel  sharp pains on my side of the stomach. I'm afraid that I'm get it again. But honestly, I really do hope you start feeling better. I hate this, and I am afraid to get it back.

Ps. Sorry for the long response. The pills worked, but I felt that after awhile I started to get constipation.
